paras: The assault on William Tinker was a knife attack on a Black bootblack by Samuel Frasier, a white man from Richmond, Virginia, at the St. James Hotel corner in Washington, D.C., on Saturday, July 2, 1881. Frasier said Tinker had cursed President Garfield; the Police Court fined him $5 or 15 days.

It occurred amid excitement in Washington over the shooting of President Garfield, which the Evening Star was covering at length. Tinker worked as a bootblack at the St. James, opposite the Baltimore and Potomac depot; Frasier was a stranger in the city from Richmond, Virginia.

Tinker testified that while he was blacking a gentleman's boots, Frasier asked if the President was dead, accused him of cursing the President, and cut at him several times with a knife, cutting his clothing. His coat, pants and shirt were cut "but not his skin." Officer Kearney arrested Frasier, who, the officer testified, said at headquarters that he would cut the heart out of any man who would curse the President.

Judge Snell heard the assault charge in the Police Court on Monday, July 4. The court found that he was "evidently acting under the general excitement" and, as no serious damage was done, fined him $5 or 15 days in jail. No report of an appeal or further proceedings was found.

Only the Washington Evening Star covered the case: an arrest item on July 3, the hearing on July 4 (repeated July 5) and a docket entry. Its headlines, "A Richmond Man Attacks a Colored Man for Cursing the President" and "The Man Who Assaulted a Boot-Black for Cursing the President," stated Frasier's claimed motive as the cause of the attack. It called Frasier "a large middle-aged white man" and Tinker "colored," but treated the affair as one of feeling over the President, not race.

Frasier's own account changed between arrest and hearing. At his arrest he denied cutting Tinker, saying he had jumped at him "intending to administer chastisement" when Tinker jumped and tore his clothing. In court he testified that Tinker had said the President "ain't as dead as he ought to be" and struck at him with his blacking-box, and that he then cut at Tinker with a knife.

bases: A single white man, Samuel Frasier, cut at a Black bootblack with a knife in a street quarrel over a remark about the wounded President; no mob or group is reported (A1, A2).
All reports come from one paper, the Washington Evening Star, though in three separately reported items (arrest A1, court hearing A2, docket A5) that agree on the core event.

accounts.label: Tinker's testimony
accounts.gist: While he was blacking a gentleman's boots, Frasier asked if the President was dead, accused him of cursing the President, pulled a knife and cut at him several times, cutting his clothing.

accounts.label: Frasier's statement at arrest
accounts.gist: Frasier denied cutting Tinker; he said Tinker was cursing and traducing President Garfield and that he jumped at him to administer chastisement, when Tinker jumped and tore his clothing.

accounts.label: Frasier's court testimony
accounts.gist: Tinker said the President 'ain't as dead as he ought to be'; when warned, Tinker got abusive and struck at him with his blacking-box, and Frasier cut at him with a knife.

accounts.label: Arresting officer
accounts.gist: Officer Kearney testified that Frasier said at headquarters he would cut the heart out of any man who would curse the President.

framing.detail: The Evening Star headlined the arrest 'A Richmond Man Attacks a Colored Man for Cursing the President' and the hearing 'The Man Who Assaulted a Boot-Black for Cursing the President', giving the assailant's claimed motive as the cause, within its columns on the shooting of the President.

versions.value: Frasier accused Tinker of cursing the President and attacked him with a knife (Tinker)
Frasier jumped at Tinker to administer chastisement for cursing the President (Frasier at arrest)
Tinker got abusive and struck at Frasier with his blacking-box first (Frasier in court)

conflicts.note: Both of Frasier's versions are his own claim; in the earlier one he says he moved on Tinker first.
